title: Grade 3 Maths — Fri, May 29
description: Word Problems — Mixed Operations — Day 5 of 5
subject: mathematics

questions.question: Riya has 35 coloured pencils. She gives 8 to her sister. How many does she have left?
questions.explanation: 35 − 8 = 27. Subtraction tells us how many are left.

questions.question: A shop sells 6 cakes every hour. How many cakes are sold in 8 hours?
There are 54 children divided equally into 9 teams. How many children per team?
Arun had ₹72. He spent ₹45 on a book. How much money does he have left?
There are 7 shelves in a library. Each shelf has 9 books. How many books are there?
Priya baked 48 cookies. She wants to share them equally among 6 friends. How many cookies does each friend get?
A school has 3 classes. Each class has 28 students. How many students are there in the school?
A train travels 120 km in the morning and 85 km in the afternoon. How far does it travel in total?
Ravi has 4 bags of marbles with 12 marbles in each bag. He gives away 15 marbles. How many does he have?
A garden has 6 rows of flowers. Each row has 7 red flowers and 3 yellow flowers. How many flowers in total?
questions.explanation: Each row has 7+3=10 flowers. 6 × 10 = 60 flowers in total.

questions.question: Meena reads 8 pages every day. How many pages does she read in a week (7 days)?
Which operation tells you how many equal groups can be made?
questions.explanation: Division splits a total into equal groups. Example: 24 ÷ 4 = 6 (how many groups of 4 in 24?).

questions.question: A farmer has 5 rows of corn plants with 14 plants in each row. How many plants are there?
Sam had 96 stickers. He shared them equally with 3 friends (each person including himself gets the same). How many does each person get?
Which word in a problem tells you to USE multiplication?
questions.explanation: Words like 'each', 'per', 'times', 'groups of', and 'rows of' are clues for multiplication.
